Silt fences, brush barriers or other measures will protect streams from sediment pollution during construction of the basin dike. Excavated slopes will be stabilized with permanent vegetation, mulch, or erosion control fabric as soon as practical.
g) Temporary and Permanent Access Roads - Cutting of temporary construction access roads through the project area will be limited. No "short-cutting" through stable areas will be allowed. This measure will prevent needless roads from becomming sources of sediment pollution. Necessary roads will be constructed to minimize erosion and to control runoff. Roads outside the reservoir will be stabilized with permanent vegetation and diversions. The roads will be closed to vehicular traffic and stabilized as soon as they are no longer needed.
Erosion and sediment pollution control during construction of the permanent access road will be accomplished using the same methods as used on the relocation of County Road 171. The route of the permanent access road is shown on drawing PBK-1014-2.
h) Discharge portal area  Runoff from the portal excavation will be directed through silt fences, brush barriers, small silt basins, or adjacent stabilized areas to remove sediment before it reaches Lake Jocassee. New slopes will be stabilized with permanent vegetation, mulch, or erosion control fabric as soon as practical upon completion.
Transmission lines  Sediment pollution from construction of transmission lines will be minimized by locating towers a sufficient distance from streams or other bodies of water to avoid problems with runoff. Low growing vegetation will not be disturbed along the water's edge or on steep slopes so that soil stability will be maintained. Selective cutting of trees will be employed in low areas where valleys can be spanned by the conductors. In the areas that require clearing for construction, the right of way will be seeded immediately with a cover crop of permanent vegetation.
8. POST CONSTRUCTION PERIOD
After construction of above-ground facilities is completed, grading and sowing of permanent vegetation will be used to stabilize exposed areas. Roads no longer in use will be stabilized and closed. The construction yard will be graded and sown with permanent vegetation to control runoff. Sediment basins no longer needed will be opened and function as flow through systems. Drawing PBK-1014-3 shows the final configuration of project facilities.
